messages:
sophia: FYI - noticed a regression after the q5 quant onboarding for orion-lite on the multilang suite. short-form zh->en and ja->en BLEU down ~2.1 overall.

taku: ugh, that's not great. same test harness as before?

sofia: yes same harness. quick numbers: baseline (float32) BLEU=32.4, q5 candidate BLEU=30.3 on the 10k shortform set.

oliver: any tokenization diffs or is it purely model output change?

sophia: small clue: token counts differ for mixed CJK+latin lines. run diff on tokenized outputs: some hair/zero-width spaces and U+2060 Word Joiner handling changed.

sophia: snippet from tokenizer dump (showing invisible chars):
```
orig: "東京Aラウンジ"  -> tokens: ["東京", "\u2006", "A", "ラウンジ"]
q5   : "東京\u206Aラウンジ" -> tokens: ["東京A", "ラウンジ"]
```
(weird mixing of U+2006 / U+206A here due to normalization heuristics)

marie: so token boundary shifts cause different BPE merges -> downstream decode shifts. makes sense.

taku: which component changed the norm? tokenizer proto bumped in model build or runtime lib?

oliver: i checked: tokenizer v2.11 pulled in a change to treat "punct+invisible" as glue for latin adjacency. committed in infra hash `a1b2c3d`. quant runtime also upgraded qoperator-v2. both landed same day.

sophia: quick bisect plan: run tokenizer-only delta on float model, then run q5 with older tokenizer. that'll tell us if it's tokenizer or quant path.

eval-bot: queued eval job: `./eval/multilang_shortform --split zh_ja_mix --model orion-lite:q5 --runs 5` (job id 6123456790)

oliver: also run with quant backend `qlegacy` to isolate qoperator-v2 changes:
```
./run_infer --model orion-lite:q5 --quant-backend qlegacy --tokenizer v2.11
```

marie: if it's tokenizer regression, we should patch normalization to fold hair/word-joiner to U+FEFF or remove before tokenization in preproc. quick patch on canary pipeline?

sophia: i tried normalizing U+2000..U+200F -> remove and reran locally. BLEU for q5 recovered ~+1.8 (so still slightly below baseline). looks like both factors combine.

taku: ok that suggests a dual cause. next steps: 1) revert tokenizer glue rule on canary, 2) test qoperator-v2 vs qlegacy on nightly, 3) add preproc normalize step to onboarding checklist.

oliver: schedule canary rollback for dedicated pool 'orion-canary' in 30m if prod metrics still green. i'll file the ops ticket.

marie: can we add a quick automated check in the onboard pipeline that compares token counts for multilang artifacts? even naive token-count delta > 0.5% flags a manual review.

sophia: good idea. i can add a lightweight check in `onboard/validate_tokens.py` and wire it into ci. minimal patch: compute mean tokens per sentence across locales and compare to baseline.

eval-bot: summary: job 6123456790 finished -> BLEU delta -1.95 vs baseline. detailed logs at https://eval.redwood/internal/6123456790 (access: eng-ml).

taku: thanks. i'll own the tokenizer revert PR if oliver gives the thumbs for canary. sophia please paste the minimal normalize patch here when ready. :thumbsup:

sophia: will do. prepping PR now and attaching run output. planning a longer 100k run overnight to check longform sensitivity.

marie: thanks all — keep thread updated. if rollback required ping #eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:
